Alloy 454 is a single-crystal nickel superalloy.
The gamma-prime phase content in Alloy 454 and Mar-M 247 is around 60%.
Alloy 454 showed a 0.2% yield strength and tensile strength equal to or greater than Mar-M 247.
Alloy 454 showed greater creep rupture strength than the reference alloys, especially at temperatures above 900°C.
The orientation dependence of tensile strength and creep resistance was most pronounced at around 760°C.
Orientations near the -111 and 011 axes showed much lower strength compared to the 001 axis.
The tensile axis orientation was determined using Laue's reverse X-ray method.
Samples were solution treated at 1280°C for 4 hours and aged at 871°C for 32 hours.
The creep testing was performed at temperatures of 760, 800, 900, 982, and 1000°C.
TEM analysis revealed differences in dislocation structures and gamma-prime deformation between different orientations.
The low creep strength near the -111 axis is attributed to the activation of {100}<110> slip systems.
The vane axis of turbine vanes in service is typically near the 001 axis.
The anisotropy is explained in terms of the activation of different slip systems and the geometric arrangement of the gamma-prime precipitates.
Alloy 454 showed a larger allowance in high strength off-axis orientation from the 001 axis compared to other alloys.
The anisotropy was most pronounced at 760°C, where the gamma-prime phase strength is at its peak.
